subject: Clearline POC: throughput intake, spike profile & success plan
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alison Park <alison@clearline.ai>; ops@clearline.ai
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-15T15:07:00Z
Subject: Clearline POC: throughput intake, spike profile & success plan

Thanks for your time today — quick recap and proposed next steps so we can turn the discovery into a scoped POC. Short version up top: we think a 2-week throughput POC focused on inference economics (latency & cost under realistic load) + correctness checks makes sense.

Key workload signals you shared (please confirm):
- Primary traffic: REST text-generation API for question-answering and summarization behind your agent platform.
- Steady-state RPS: ~12 req/s baseline.
- Median tokens per request (input+output): ~220 tokens.
- 95th percentile token length: ~1,100 tokens (rare long summaries).
- Concurrency: 40 concurrent connections observed during day, but only ~8 heavy model requests concurrently in normal hours.
- Burst behavior: short spikes to 200–250 RPS during end-of-day batch replays + marketing events (~30–90s).

POC objective and success criteria (proposal):
1) Performance: 95th percentile token latency < 180ms for the bulk of traffic (requests <=600 tokens) and graceful degradation for long tails (<=1,500 tokens) with fallbacks.
2) Stability: no more than 1 request error rate above 5xx per 100k tokens over the test window.
3) Cost visibility: per-token cost estimate with Redwood Optimize recommendations; target a <20% increase over current cloud-hosted baseline.
4) Functional correctness: end-to-end QA on 8 canonical prompts (we'll exchange labeled expected outputs).

Proposed evaluation plan & timeline:
- Nov 16: Clearline uploads sample traffic + 48 hours of logs and reply with the sample CSV (we attached a template).
- Nov 18–19: Redwood runs ingest + baseline characterization (RPS distribution, length histograms, KV cache hit expectation).
- Nov 20–Nov 30: Two-week POC window where we run production-backend-like traffic (replay + synthetic bursts) and measure metrics.
- Dec 1: Readout meeting and next-step recommendations (scale/quantization/production rollout).

Owners:
- Redwood AE: Soojin Lee (point-of-contact, escalations).
- Redwood SE: Karthik Iyer (test harness, traffic replay, perf tuning).
- Customer POC lead: Alison Park (data & acceptance).

Attachments: clearline_sample_queries.csv (template) and a draft POC SOW (see attached stub).

Please confirm the workload numbers above or flag differences. If you agree, we’ll send a short SOW and calendar invite for the ingest window.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai
[Attachment: clearline_sample_queries.csv (csv)]
[Attachment: clearline_poc_sow_draft.pdf (pdf)]

From: Alison Park <alison@clearline.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@clearline.ai; Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-16T09:34:00Z
Subject: Re: Clearline POC: throughput intake, spike profile & success plan

Thanks, Soojin — that lines up well with what we saw. Quick clarifications:
- The 200–250 RPS spikes are real but usually only last 45–75 seconds; they come from our nightly agent syncs.
- The 95th percentile token length is closer to 950 tokens across real traffic; the 1,100 number was from a heavy internal analytic job.
- We can provide 72 hours of request logs and a 2,000-sample labeled set for correctness tests by EOD Nov 17.

One more ask: can Redwood simulate our end-of-day bursts (200 RPS) with a 60s hold window so we can validate autoscaling and graceful fallback? Also include an estimate of the expected additional cost for the 2-week POC so our finance lead can sign off.

I’ll loop in procurement if the SOW looks standard.

— Alison
Alison Park | Head of Platform Engineering, Clearline AI
[External attachment: clearline_logs_72h_sample.tar.gz (stub)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alison Park <alison@clearline.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-17T18:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Clearline POC: throughput intake, spike profile & success plan

Great — thanks for confirming, Alison. We can definitely run a 60s sustained burst to 200 RPS during the POC window and will include two patterns:
1) Synthetic burst: constant 200 RPS for 60s using a token-length distribution sampled from your 72h logs.
2) Mixed burst: 200 RPS that includes a 10% fraction of long-tail requests (~900–1,200 tokens) to stress KV cache and tokenization.

Quick notes on measurement and tooling:
- We’ll capture token-level latency histograms, per-request cost, and KV cache hit/miss ratios.
- P95 latency target we’ll track separately for short (<600 tokens) and long (>600 tokens) cohorts.
- We’ll provide a per-day dashboard link and an anonymized replay artifact so Clearline can re-run tests.

Cost estimate for the two-week POC (rough):
- Baseline replay at observed steady-state: ~$1,200 (compute + infra).
- Burst injection runs and longer-tail tests: additional ~$800.
- Total POC estimate: ~$2,000 (this is an initial estimate; final SOW will list detailed line items).

Action items I’ll take after we get the logs:
- Convert your 72h logs into our load-replay harness.
- Produce expected RPS/concurrency profile and an ingest report by Nov 19 EOD.
- Share a link to the dashboard + replay artifact.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: poc_replay_readme.md (txt)]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alison Park <alison@clearline.ai>, procurement@clearline.ai
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-18T11:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Clearline POC: throughput intake, spike profile & success plan

Alison — thanks for the quick turnaround. We’ll proceed on the timeline below once we have your 72-hour logs and the labeled sample set: final ingest by Nov 18 EOD, replay characterization Nov 18–19, POC window Nov 20–Dec 3.

Next steps:
- Alison / Clearline: drop logs + labeled set into the Drive link (or send S3/transfer details) and confirm procurement contact.
- Soojin: send SOW + calendar invites for the ingest/readout meetings by EOD Nov 18.
- Karthik: start converting logs to replay harness once available; produce expected RPS histogram and token-length CDF.

Acceptance criteria recap (for the SOW):
- P95 latency <180ms for short cohort (<600 tokens).
- Latency during burst: system remains available with a clear fallback path (e.g., lower-accuracy model or queueing) and no more than 2% 5xx rate attributable to capacity.
- Customer signoff on correctness tests for the labeled sample set (>=90% pass on core prompts).

If procurement needs a PO or specific billing terms we can start that flow in parallel — Monica, can you take point on billing items?

I'll attach the SOW draft in a follow-up and send invites.

Thanks all — excited to get this moving.
Soojin
Soojin Lee | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
